THE HEADLINES::

 

  1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi to hold talks with Acting Head of State of Principality of Liechtenstein Hereditary Prince Alois in New Delhi today.

 

  1. Prime Minister to also inaugurate Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026 in New Delhi.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Acting Head of State of the Principality of Liechtenstein Hereditary Prince Alois will hold bilateral meeting in New Delhi today. The acting Head of State of the Principality of Liechtenstein who is on a three-day visit to India arrived in New Delhi yesterday from Vadodara. He is accompanied by his spouse Princess Sophie and a high-level official as well as a business delegation comprising top industry leaders.

 

“Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Acting Head of State of the Principality of Liechtenstein will discuss on cooperation in various areas including trade and investment, science, technology and innovation and people-to-people exchanges. They will also exchange views on regional and global developments. Prince Alois will be accorded ceremonial reception at the forecourt of Rashtrapati Bhavan this morning. He will also meet President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan this evening who will also host an official banquet in the honour of the visiting dignitary. External Affairs Minister Dr. S Jaishankar will also call on Prince Alois. This is the second visit of Prince Alois to India in 2026. He earlier visited New Delhi in February this year to attend the AI Impact Summit. Ministry of External Affairs said that the visit is expected to provide further impetus to the growing engagement between India and Liechtenstein, particularly since operationalization of India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement last year. With Anupam Mishra, Rishu Jaiswal, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. The three-day conclave will bring together leading scientists, researchers, academicians, policymakers, industry leaders, startups and international experts to deliberate on emerging technologies and India’s science, technology and innovation priorities.

 

“The deliberations will span 12 thematic areas, including artificial intelligence, biotechnology, advanced materials, manufacturing, healthcare, energy, climate and ocean sciences. Discussions will focus on research priorities, national capabilities and translating scientific advances into practical applications. The Conclave will also feature an extensive technology and innovation exhibition showcasing indigenous scientific achievements and emerging technologies. It will include around 150 deep-tech startup stalls, which will highlight technological developments and their potential applications across sectors. The Conclave will also use thematic videos, technology demonstrations, documentaries, informational kiosks and augmented and virtual reality experiences to enhance engagement with scientific developments and their real-world applications. Anupam Mishra, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The Election Commission has defended its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls before the Supreme Court, maintaining that the exercise was authorised by law and the relevant orders were approved unanimously by all three members of the Commission. Rejecting the allegations that Form 6 had been amended, the poll panel said that no changes were made to the statutory Form 6 used for voter registration. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant is scheduled to hear on Tuesday petitions against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the decisions taken by the poll panel during the SIR. In a counter affidavit, the poll body sought summary dismissal of the petitions and called the allegations misconceived which rested on a single newspaper report. It said the affidavit itself has been approved for filing by a unanimous decision of all three members of the Commission.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The counting of votes has begun for 11 MLC seats in Uttar Pradesh, eight in Bihar, five in Maharashtra and four in Karnataka. The voting took place on October 23 for the biennial elections to the Legislative Council from graduate and teachers’ constituencies in these 4 states.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Akashvani will organise the 67th edition of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Lecture series today. Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shivraj Singh Chouhan will deliver the lecture. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting informed that the recording of the Lecture will be broadcast on the Sardar Patel Jayanti on 31st of this month on the entire Akashvani Network at 9.30 P.M.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Cyclone Arnab has intensified into severe cyclonic storm over Bay of Bengal and is likely to further strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm by this evening. The cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal is moving towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, with landfall expected tomorrow morning.

 

 Odisha is bracing for heavy to extremely heavy rainfall, particularly in its southern districts, as the storm approaches the eastern coastline. The State Government has intensified preparedness, while several train services have been cancelled or curtailed as a precaution.

 

“Rain has started in southern Odisha, while coastal districts are witnessing cloudy skies as the cyclone moves closer to the eastern coast. The India Meteorological Department has warned of extremely heavy rainfall in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts tomorrow. Heavy rain may trigger waterlogging, flash floods and landslides, while strong winds could damage power lines and disrupt communication. The State Government has intensified preparedness, with rescue teams on standby and ministers assigned to monitor vulnerable districts. Educational institutions in six districts will remain closed tomorrow. Meanwhile, Railways have cancelled several services and curtailed others, including the Hirakhand Express, which will terminate at Rayagada instead of Jagdalpur. Passengers have been advised to check the latest train status before travelling. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.”

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Cyclone Arnab is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast near Yanam, between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, by tomorrow morning. The storm is likely to bring winds of 115 to 125 kilometres per hour, with gusts reaching 140 kilometres per hour.

 

“The Andhra Pradesh government has intensified precautionary measures to protect lives and property. National and State Disaster Response Force teams have been deployed in cyclone-affected districts, while additional teams, rescue boats and tree-clearing units are on standby. Authorities have identified cyclone shelters, activated control rooms and appointed nodal officers to coordinate emergency operations. Twenty-seven crore rupees have been released for relief and preparedness measures. People living in low-lying and at-risk areas are being shifted to safer places. Arrangements are being made for food, drinking water, medical care and sanitation at relief centres. Emergency teams are ready to restore electricity, clear roads and maintain essential services. Beaches have been closed, and fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea. People have been urged to follow official warnings and safety instructions. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Union Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas Hardeep Singh Puri will be the chief guest at 29th Energy Technology Meet being organized in Goa from today. The event will go on till October 29, at the ONGC Advanced Training Institute. Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) will co-host the prestigious three-day national event. It also incorporates an R&D Conclave by the Federation of Indian Petroleum Industry.

 

“The theme of conclave is “Accelerating Energy Innovation: From Research to Commercialisation,”. It aims to bring together over 1,500 domain experts, scientists, and delegates from India and overseas. The discussions will focus on petrochemical technologies, green hydrogen value chains, synthetic aviation fuels, bio-refineries, and carbon capture solutions. The summit comes at a pivotal time as the country accelerates its energy transition roadmap. It aims to serve Panchamrit action plan to reach net-zero emissions by 2070. The meet will feature technical presentations, panel interactions, digital poster sessions, and product exhibitions aimed at fostering indigenous innovations, enhancing energy security, and driving sustainable refining practices. Mahesh Chopade, Akashvani News, Panaji”.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Israel will go to polls today to elect a new Parliament. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking to retain power amid public debate over the government’s handling of 2023 Hamas attack, subsequent wars and its domestic and foreign policies. The election is widely viewed as a test of Netanyahu’s leadership, with opposition figures, including former military chief Gadi Eisenkot and former prime minister Naftali Bennett, seeking to challenge his right-wing coalition.

 Netanyahu, leader of the right-wing Likud party, has served as prime minister for nearly 19 years across three separate periods since 1996.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

The 9th Hero Hockey Men’s Asian Champions Trophy 2026 will start today in Punjab. The opening ceremony and league match of this week-long hockey extravaganza will be held at the Olympian Surjit Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar. Six leading hockey nations including host India, Malaysia, China, Japan, South Korea, and Bangladesh are participating in this first major continental hockey tournament being organized in Punjab. Akashvani’s all IndraDhanush Channels along with Jalandhar’s Primary Channel will broadcast live commentary of matches played by India and semi-finals and final as well. Entry to the venues is free.

 

“Olympian Surjit Hockey Stadium, Jalandhar and Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium, Mohali, both have been renovated as per world-standards and are ready for the matches. Starting from today, there will be three-matches on each day, including matches under flood-lights, till November 2nd at Jalandhar. The final and semi-finals will be played at the Mohali stadium on November 4th and 5th. The pool matches would start with the opening match between India and Bangladesh under flood lights. Whereas two matches between Malaysia and China and Japan v/s South Korea will be played during the day. The teams have already reached Punjab and were given a warm traditional Punjabi welcome. The glittering ‘Hero Asian Champions Trophy-2026’ has also reached Jalandhar after its week-long tour of various districts, which is the dream of every team competing in this prestigious championship. Rajesh Bali, Akashvani News, Jalandhar.”

In Men’s Cricket, third T20 International between India and New Zealand will be played today in Wellington. The match will start at 12:30 PM IST.

 

India have won the opening two matches against the hosts, and put themselves in a strong position to secure the series. A win today will seal the T20 International series for the visitors.

 

Heavy rain has been lashing parts of Wellington city ahead of the match.

Olympic medallist Mirabai Chanu will lead India’s challenge at the 2026 World Weightlifting Championships, which will begin today at Ningbo Olympic Sports Center in China. The championships will mark the first of 10 qualifying competitions on the road to 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

  2. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar says, use of terrorism as instrument of statecraft is unacceptable, and it can never be justified or rationalised.

The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum will commence in New Delhi from today. The theme of the two-day event is “Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development.” Prime Minister Narendra Modi will grace the event and will meet the leaders of the visiting delegations. Eleven BRICS Member countries and 10 Partner countries have been invited for the event. Parliamentary delegations from these countries will participate in the meeting. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

         

 

 

“Lok Sabha Speaker and Chairperson of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum Om Birla will preside over the proceedings and hold discussions with leaders of the visiting delegations during the bilateral meetings. Building on the legacy of the BRICS Parliamentary Forum, the 12th Forum aims to foster consensus-based dialogue through four High-Level Sessions based on Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. A dedicated meeting of the Chairs of International Affairs Committees of Parliaments of BRICS Member and Partner countries will be held to deliberate on parliamentary diplomacy, capacity-building, and sharing of best practices. The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum, being hosted by India, will provide an opportunity to advance parliamentary diplomacy, strengthen democratic institutions, and promote cooperation among member and partner countries. Akshit Vedyan, AKASHVANI NEWS, DELHI.”

 

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

Lok Sabha Speaker and Chairperson of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum Om Birla today said that BRICS has evolved into an influential anchor of Global South and a driving force for multilateral architecture. In an article for a daily newspaper, Mr Birla said that the growing engagement among the BRICS countries has also strengthened its parliamentary dimension through the BRICS Parliamentary Forum.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has said that the use of terrorism as an instrument of statecraft is simply unacceptable, and it can never be justified or rationalised. He said, terrorism continues because not all states display zero tolerance for the menace. Dr Jaishankar was addressing an event held in New Delhi to mark 75th anniversary of Chinmaya Mission. He said, the world must develop sharper awareness about this common threat, and it must come together with stronger resolve to counter terrorism in all its forms and manifestations.

 

 

 

         

 

 

He underlined the importance of peace, especially amid the ongoing conflicts in the world, and cautioned that war anywhere threatens peace everywhere. Dr Jaishankar cited the two major conflicts going on in the world, in Ukraine and in West Asia, and said societies and economies and people far away who have little say in the matter are actually paying the cost.

 

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

ISRO Chairman V Narayanan has said that India will expand its space operations significantly with four functional launch pads by the year 2029. Mr. Narayanan said, these include a 2 thousand acre dedicated Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) complex at Kulasekarapattinam in Tuticorin district of Tamil Nadu and a third launch pad at Sriharikota, to meet the global demand for satellite launches. He was addressing convocation of a private university at Porur near Chennai.

 

 

 

         

 

 

The ISRO chief said that the upcoming Kulasekarapattinam spaceport facility will feature crucial infrastructure such as integration buildings, launch pads, rail-track systems, telemetry, tracking, and command systems.

 

 

         

 

Mr. Narayanan stated that ISRO plans to conduct the first uncrewed Gaganyaan test within the next two months, followed by two subsequent uncrewed tests before the crewed mission.

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will hold nationwide protests at all its state headquarters today against Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge for allegedly making derogatory remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s late father.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

Union Home Minister and Senior BJP Leader Amit Shah has hit out at Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge over his alleged remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s father. In a social media post, Mr Shah said that this is not the first time that the Congress party has used abusive language against the family of Prime Minister Modi. The Home Minister alleged that the leaders of Congress party have hurled insults at Mr Modi’s revered mother and mocked his poverty. He further alleged that the Congress party keeps crossing the limits of indecency every day under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi. Mr Shah said that the persistent electoral defeats over the last 12 years have led to such deep-seated frustration and despair within the Congress party.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to the citizens on the occasion of Maharishi Valmiki Jayanti today. In a social media post, the President said that everyone effortlessly receives teachings on duty, good conduct, selfless action, the welfare of others, friendship, sacrifice, righteousness, and devotion from the epic Ramayana composed by Maharishi Valmiki.

 

 

         

 

 

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has also extended his wishes to the citizens on the occasion. He said that the noble thoughts of Maharishi Valmiki have been the foundational elements of Indian culture and heritage, which will continue to nurture and flourish the nation in every era. Mr Modi added that Maharishi Valmiki’s invaluable messages for humanity will forever serve as guiding lights for the people of this country.

<><><> 

         

 

 

Vice President C P Radhakrishnan will be on a two day visit to Andhra Pradesh beginning today. During the visit, the Vice-President will attend the 40th Anniversary Celebrations of Dr NTR University of Health Sciences in Vijayawada as a chief guest.

India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that the Deep Depression over Bay of Bengal will intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm today. IMD has advised the fisherman not to venture into West central and adjoining Northwest and Southwest Bay of Bengal during the next two days.

 

 

Talking to Akashvani News, Director General of IMD, Dr Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said, due to influence of depression the sea condition is very rough and will deteriorate further. He said that the wind speed may lead to large scale damage of structures and standing crops. He said that heavy to extremely heavy rainfall may hit parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh during the next two days. Dr Mohapatra added that due to heavy rainfall can cause flooding in low-lying areas and landslides in hilly areas and urged the people living in these regions to be cautious. 

 

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

 

Odisha government has stepped up preparedness, deploying eight ministers to oversee arrangements in vulnerable districts as heavy rainfall and strong winds are forecast. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

 

 

 

“The India Meteorological Department has forecast that Cyclone Arnab will intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by tomorrow morning and a very severe cyclonic storm as it approaches the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday. In Odisha, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has assigned eight ministers, including the two Deputy Chief Ministers, to oversee preparedness in Koraput, Rayagada, Kandhamal, Ganjam, Nabarangpur, Malkangiri, Kalahandi and Gajapati districts. Red warnings have been issued for all the southern districts for very heavy rainfall from tomorrow till Thursday. Some coastal districts will also experience very heavy rainfall under the impact of Cyclone Arnab. The state government has stepped up disaster-response arrangements, directed officials to remain alert and prioritised the safety of people in vulnerable areas. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.”

 

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

 

Our Visakhapatnam correspondent Satyanarayana has filed this report on weather condition in Andhra Pradesh:

 

 

“The Andhra Pradesh and adjoining South Odisha coasts have been placed under an Orange Alert as a Deep Depression over the Eastcentral and Southeast Bay of Bengal rapidly intensifies into a major storm system. Landfall is expected by the forenoon of October 28, crossing the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam with destructive sustained wind speeds of 115-125 kmph, gusting up to 140 kmph. In anticipation of the cyclone’s impact, the IMD has warned of widespread heavy rainfall over the next two days and has urged the public to remain on high alert. Residents are strongly advised to postpone any travel plans, while fishermen have been strictly ordered not to venture into the sea. To counter the threat, the Andhra Pradesh state government is actively coordinating across all departments to deploy emergency resources, secure vulnerable areas, and prevent loss of life and property. Satyanarayana, Akashvani News, Visakhapatnam.”

In Brazil, Leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has defeated right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil’s intense presidential race. With this victory, Lula has become the only politician in modern Brazilian history who successfully rebound and win the second round after falling behind in the first. A report:

 

 

         

 

 

“Incumbent Lula won the final runoff election with 51 percent of the vote and more than 51.49 million ballots. Meanwhile, Bolsonaro received 48.68 percent of the vote, which amounted to 48.8 million ballots. Just over 2.6 million votes separated the two candidates. Because of the close and highly contested race, voting stations across the country remained open two hours longer than originally planned.

         

 

 

The former metalworker union leader, at the age of 80 will be sworn into office on 5th of January next year, breaking his own record as the oldest president to take the oath of office since Brazil returned to a democracy. This victory marks an unprecedented fourth non-consecutive term for Lula, who has run for the presidency a total of seven times. KAUMUDEE PAREEK FOR AKASHVANI NEWS DELHI.”

In Women’s Cricket, India defeated Zimbabwe by 121 runs in the second One Day International (ODI) in Vadodara last night, taking an unassailable 2-nil lead in the three-match series. Chasing a target of 329 runs, Zimbabwe were bowled out for 207 in 48.5 overs. Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano top scored with 46 runs off 57 balls. For India, Vaishnavi Sharma took four wickets, while Deepti Sharma claimed three.

 

 

<><><> 

         

 

In Tennis, India’s top-ranked doubles player, Yuki Bhambri with his American partner Ryan Seggerman clinched the Almaty Open title in Kazakhstan yesterday. The fourth-seeded Indo-American pair defeated top seeds Lucas Miedler and Neil Oberleitner of Austria 7-6, 6-7, 10-2 in the final of ATP 250 tournament.

International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) has announced that Ahmedabad will host the Senior World Weightlifting Championships in 2029. This will be the first time that India hosts the senior edition of the prestigious global event. The decision was taken at the IWF Executive Board meeting held in Ningbo, China.
